name: LPC812M101JDH20J
title: LPC81xM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller family with 4 kB to 16 kB flash and 1 kB to 4 kB SRAM
summary: A small Cortex-M0+ microcontroller family running at up to 30 MHz from one 1.8 V to 3.6 V supply, with up to 16 kB flash and 4 kB SRAM. A switch matrix puts the USART, SPI, I2C, timer and comparator functions on any I/O pin. It starts from a 12 MHz internal RC oscillator, needs no crystal, and has four low-power modes down to Deep power-down at 170 nA typical. LPC812M101JDH20 is the 16 kB, TSSOP20 member with 18 GPIO, three USARTs and two SPI interfaces.
key_figures: 16 kB flash, 4 kB SRAM, 8 kB boot ROM
1.4 mA typ at 12 MHz, 3.3 mA typ at 30 MHz (default mode, 3.3 V)
18 GPIO, 5 V tolerant except PIO0_6; 20 mA source on four pins, 20 mA sink on two open-drain pins
3 USART, 2 SPI, 1 I2C (Fast-mode Plus on PIO0_10/PIO0_11)
1 comparator with 32-step ladder and 0.9 V reference

pins.name: PIO0_17
pins.function: General-purpose I/O, 5 V tolerant.

pins.name: PIO0_13
pins.function: General-purpose I/O. 5 V tolerant, high-drive output.

pins.name: PIO0_12
pins.function: General-purpose I/O, 5 V tolerant, high-drive output. ISP entry pin on SO20, TSSOP20, TSSOP16 and XSON16 parts from chip revision 4C: pulled LOW through reset, it enters the ISP handler.

pins.name: RESET/PIO0_5
pins.function: RESET, active LOW, is the function selected out of reset: a LOW pulse of 50 ns or longer resets the chip, returns I/O and peripherals to their defaults and starts code at address 0. It does not work in Deep power-down, where it needs an external pull-up. If neither external reset nor Deep power-down is used it may be left open, or used as PIO0_5 or for a movable function. LOW on this pin at power-up selects JTAG boundary scan; HIGH selects SWD. 5 V tolerant.

pins.name: PIO0_4/WAKEUP/TRST
pins.function: General-purpose I/O. Carries USART0 transmit (U0_TXD) in ISP mode and TRST in boundary-scan mode. WAKEUP: a LOW pulse of 50 ns or longer brings the chip out of Deep power-down; it must be held HIGH by an external resistor before that mode is entered, and a pin used this way must not carry a movable function. The wake-up function can be turned off when the WKT low-power oscillator does the waking. 5 V tolerant.

pins.name: SWCLK/PIO0_3/TCK
pins.function: SWCLK, the Serial Wire Debug clock, is the function selected out of reset. Can be switched to general-purpose I/O PIO0_3; TCK in boundary-scan mode. 5 V tolerant, high-drive output.

pins.name: SWDIO/PIO0_2/TMS
pins.function: SWDIO, the Serial Wire Debug data line, is the function selected out of reset. Can be switched to general-purpose I/O PIO0_2; TMS in boundary-scan mode. 5 V tolerant, high-drive output.

pins.name: PIO0_11
pins.function: General-purpose I/O with a true open-drain output, the partner of PIO0_10 for full-specification I2C0 (including Fast-mode Plus). Needs an external pull-up; floats when unpowered. Tolerates 5.5 V whether VDD is present or not.

pins.name: PIO0_10
pins.function: General-purpose I/O with a true open-drain output (needs an external pull-up). The pin for I2C0 when the full I2C-bus specification is needed: I2C standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus with high-current sink. Floats when the chip is unpowered, so it leaves the bus alone. Not suited to fast signals such as SPI or USART. Tolerates 5.5 V whether VDD is present or not.

tables.title: Device revision marking
notes: Top-side marking: four lines, LPC81x / xxxxx / xxxxxxxx / xxYWWxR[x]. The last two characters of the last line, xR, give the boot code version and device revision; Y is the year and WW the week of manufacture.
On TSSOP16 parts the last line holds only the date code xxYWW.

notes: Cb: total capacitance of one bus line, pF.
tHD;DAT is taken from the falling edge of SCL, tSU;DAT to the rising edge of SCL; both apply to data and to the acknowledge.
A device must hold SDA internally for at least 300 ns after VIH(min) of SCL so the undefined part of SCL's falling edge is bridged.

Bus lines may take up to 300 ns to fall; the SDA output stage itself is held to 250 ns, leaving room for series protection resistors between the pins and the bus. In Fast-mode Plus the output stage and the bus share the same fall time, so series resistors must be allowed for in the timing.

The largest tHD;DAT may be 3.45 µs (Standard-mode) and 0.9 µs (Fast-mode), but must undercut the largest tVD;DAT or tVD;ACK by one transition time; it matters only where SCL LOW is not stretched. A device that stretches SCL must have data valid one set-up time before it lets the clock go.

A Fast-mode device on a Standard-mode bus must meet tSU;DAT = 250 ns; if it stretches SCL LOW it must put the next bit on SDA tr(max) + tSU;DAT = 1000 + 250 = 1250 ns before releasing SCL, and the acknowledge must meet the same set-up time.

circuits.title: SWD debug connector
circuits.description: A standard Serial Wire Debug connector wired to the chip: the connector's VTREF pin connects to the board supply VDD, SWDIO and SWCLK go straight to the chip's SWDIO/PIO0_2 and SWCLK/PIO0_3, the connector's nRESET drives the chip's RESET pin, and GND is the board ground. PIO0_12 is brought out as the ISP entry line.
notes: On the DIP8 part and on chip revisions 1A and 2A the ISP entry pin is PIO0_1 instead of PIO0_12.

circuits.title: External clock into XTALIN (oscillator slave mode)
circuits.description: An external clock drives XTALIN through a 100 pF coupling capacitor Ci. A second capacitor Cg from XTALIN to ground forms a divider with Ci, scaling the input by Ci/(Ci + Cg) so the pin stays within its 1.8 V limit. XTALOUT may be left open.

parts.note: chosen to bring the clock amplitude within 200 mV(RMS) to 1000 mV(RMS) at XTALIN

circuits.title: Crystal on XTALIN and XTALOUT
circuits.description: A fundamental-mode crystal between XTALIN and XTALOUT with a load capacitor from each pin to ground. The feedback resistor is inside the chip, so the crystal and CX1, CX2 are the only outside parts. CX1 and CX2 follow the crystal's load capacitance and frequency.

operation.text: An ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU running at up to 30 MHz, with up to 16 kB of flash and 4 kB of SRAM. Around it: CRC engine, I2C, as many as three USARTs and two SPI interfaces, a multi-rate timer, a self wake-up timer, the SCTimer/PWM, one analog comparator, a pattern match engine on the pin interrupts, and up to 18 GPIO pins whose functions are placed by a switch matrix.

Single-cycle multiplier and single-cycle I/O port; NVIC; SysTick; SWD debug and JTAG boundary scan; Micro Trace Buffer. Flash written and erased in 64-byte pages. ROM holds the boot loader, USART and I2C drivers, power profiles, and flash IAP/ISP. Four pins can source 20 mA; the two true open-drain pins can sink 20 mA. Unique serial number per device. One supply. Operating range -40 °C to 105 °C, but -40 °C to 85 °C for the DIP8 part. Packages DIP8, TSSOP16, SO20, TSSOP20 and XSON16.
8/16-bit applications, consumer, climate control, lighting, motor control, fire and security.

The Cortex-M0+ has a two-stage pipeline, four breakpoints and two watchpoints for SWD. Flash: up to 16 kB, 64-byte pages. SRAM: up to 4 kB. An 8 kB ROM carries the boot loader and the APIs for ISP and IAP flash programming, power profiles and PLL setup, USART and I2C drivers.

The NVIC handles 32 vectored interrupts, of which up to 8 are external inputs taken from any GPIO pin, with four priority levels, SVCall and PendSV software interrupts and a relocatable vector table. Each peripheral has one interrupt line, which may gather several flags. Up to eight pins, whatever their function, can interrupt on level, rising, falling or both edges.
24-bit system tick timer in the Cortex-M0+, meant for a periodic exception such as every 10 ms.

IOCON sets each PIO0_n pin (other than the true open-drain PIO0_10 and PIO0_11): weak pull-up and pull-down on or off; pseudo open-drain mode (cannot be pulled above VDD, and not 5 V tolerant with VDD = 0); a programmable input glitch filter clocked from one of the IOCON clock dividers, or bypassed; input inversion; hysteresis on or off; analog mode on mixed pins, which disconnects the digital side. On PIO0_10 and PIO0_11 it selects standard digital, I2C standard/fast, or I2C Fast-mode Plus drive. A standard pad also offers a repeater mode on its input.

Movable functions (USART, SPI, SCT, I2C, comparator output, CLKOUT, pattern match output) can be placed on any pin but supply and ground. Fixed-pin functions such as XTALIN, XTALOUT, the comparator inputs, SWD and RESET belong to one pin each and are only switched on or off; when off, the pin can take a movable function. GPIO is a fixed-pin function, on by default except on PIO0_2, PIO0_3 and PIO0_5.

GPIO registers sit on the Cortex-M0+ single-cycle I/O bus, so pins can toggle at up to 15 MHz. A whole port can be written in one instruction, with mask, set and clear, and each bit has its own direction. After reset every I/O is an input with its pull-up on, apart from the true open-drain pins.

Up to eight pins, chosen through SYSCON from any digital pin, become separate edge- or level-sensitive NVIC interrupts that can wake the part from Sleep, Deep-sleep and Power-down. The same eight inputs can feed a boolean expression of levels and transitions; each product term raises its own interrupt and a match can also signal RXEV to the CPU (and drive a pin). Pattern matches do not wake the part.

Every USART pin is movable. Up to 1.875 Mbit/s asynchronous and 10 Mbit/s synchronous on any digital pin except PIO0_10 and PIO0_11. 7, 8 or 9 data bits, 1 or 2 stop bits; synchronous master or slave; 9-bit multidrop addressing (RS-485 with software address match and direction control); odd, even or no parity; single transmit and receive buffers; RTS/CTS flow control; break; three-sample voting on receive with a noise flag; baud rate generator plus one fractional divider shared by all USARTs; loopback modes; ROM driver. USART0 and USART1 are on every part; USART2 is on LPC812M101JTB16, LPC812M101JDH16 and LPC812M101JDH20.

Every SPI pin is movable. Up to 30 Mbit/s as master and 25 Mbit/s as slave on any digital pin except PIO0_10 and PIO0_11. Frames of 1 to 16 bits in hardware, longer in software; master or slave; transmit without reading; control bits can be written with the data; one slave select of selectable polarity. TI SSI and Microwire formats are not supported. SPI0 is on every part; SPI1 is on LPC812M101JDH16, LPC812M101JDH20 and LPC812M101JTB16.

Standard and Fast mode up to 400 kbit/s; master, slave and monitor; multi-master; several slave addresses in hardware, one of them maskable or as a range; 10-bit addressing with software help; SMBus; ROM driver. The functions can go on any pin, but only PIO0_10 and PIO0_11 meet the whole I2C-bus specification: on them the bus stays undisturbed when the chip is unpowered and Fast-mode Plus runs up to 1 Mbit/s.

Two 16-bit counters or one 32-bit counter, clocked by the bus clock or an input, counting up or up-down, with a state variable so behaviour can follow a sequence across counter cycles. Events come from matches, inputs or outputs, in a given state and count direction, and drive outputs, interrupts, state changes and counter limit, halt, start and stop. Match 0 can be the automatic limit. Resources: 4 inputs, 4 outputs, 5 match/capture registers, 6 events, 2 states. All its pins are movable.
Four independent 31-bit down-counting channels, each with its own interval, for repeating interrupts; repeat, one-shot and bus-stall modes.

A 24-bit timer with prescaler, clocked from the dedicated watchdog oscillator, that resets the chip (or interrupts) if it is not fed in time. Optional window demands feeding between a minimum and maximum time; optional warning interrupt before time-out. Once enabled by software it can only be turned off by a hardware or watchdog reset. A wrong feed sequence resets or interrupts. A flag records a watchdog reset.

A 32-bit loadable down-counter in the always-on domain: loading a non-zero value starts it, and reaching zero raises an interrupt or wake-up. Clocked by the IRC or by the low-power oscillator; the latter runs in Deep power-down, so the timer can wake the part from any reduced power mode or serve as a general timer.

Compares pin voltages and internal voltages, with hysteresis of 0 mV, 10 mV (± 5 mV), 20 mV (± 10 mV) or 40 mV (± 20 mV). Either input can take VDD or VDDCMP (PIO0_6), the band-gap reference, or a 32-step voltage ladder fed from VDDCMP or the 3.3 V supply; the ladder can be powered down separately. The level output is the movable function ACMP_O and can also feed an SCT input; edges raise an NVIC interrupt. Inputs and reference are switched onto PIO0_0, PIO0_1 and PIO0_6 by the switch matrix. After power-up or a change of input channel the ladder output needs its settling time before it is used as a reference.

Four oscillators: the crystal oscillator (SysOsc, 1 MHz to 25 MHz); the 12 MHz IRC, trimmed to 1.5 % over voltage and temperature; a 10 kHz low-power oscillator (± 40 %) for the WKT, able to run in every low-power mode; and the watchdog oscillator, programmable from 9.4 kHz to 2.3 MHz with ± 40 % spread over process. After any reset the part runs from the IRC until software chooses otherwise, so no crystal is needed and the boot loader runs at a known rate. The IRC or SysOsc can clock the CPU directly or through the PLL.
An external clock up to 25 MHz can come in on CLKIN, which follows the digital I/O characteristics, or as a 1.8 V signal on XTALIN to the system oscillator.

Takes 10 MHz to 25 MHz in, multiplies by an integer 1 to 32 with a current-controlled oscillator running 156 MHz to 320 MHz, and divides the output by 2, 4, 8 or 16, which gives a 50 % duty cycle. It is off and bypassed after reset; software sets it up, waits for lock (nominally 100 µs) and then switches to it. It can run from the system oscillator, CLKIN or the IRC.
CLKOUT, through its own divider, can carry the IRC, the system oscillator, the watchdog oscillator or the main clock; the switch matrix routes it to whichever digital pin is wanted.

Power can be traded against speed by changing clock source, PLL and CPU clock divider, and by gating the clock of each unused peripheral; some peripherals have their own divider. ROM power profile calls set the chip for default, CPU performance, efficiency or low-current operation and choose PLL settings for a given clock.
The core clock stops; peripherals keep running and their interrupts, or a reset, resume execution. No special sequence is needed to resume.

Core asleep and every clock off apart from the IRC (its output off) and, if chosen, the watchdog or low-power oscillator; analog blocks off, flash in standby. The watchdog oscillator and BOD can stay on for timed wake-up and brown-out protection. Wakes on reset, pin interrupt inputs, a watchdog interrupt, or interrupts from the USART (synchronous slave), SPI or I2C (slave); the source must be enabled in a SYSCON wake-up register and the NVIC. Short wake-up time.
As Deep-sleep but the IRC and the flash are off too; only the watchdog or low-power oscillator may run, with the BOD if wanted. Same wake-up sources. Lower current than Deep-sleep, longer wake-up.

Everything is off except the WAKEUP pin and, if enabled, the self wake-up timer; four general-purpose registers keep their contents. Wakes on the WAKEUP pin or on WKT time-out, then runs a full reset. A lock bit in the PMU can forbid this mode so that the watchdog or BOD always keeps running. WAKEUP needs an external pull-up holding it HIGH, and RESET should be pulled HIGH so it does not float.

Four sources: the RESET pin (Schmitt-trigger input), the watchdog, power-on reset and the BOD. A LOW pulse of 50 ns or longer on RESET resets the part. Once the supply is usable any reset starts the IRC and the flash controller; on release, execution starts at address 0 from the boot block's reset vector with every register at its reset value. RESET needs an external pull-up in Deep power-down.

The VDD pin is watched against up to four levels. Falling below a chosen level raises an interrupt to the NVIC, also readable from a status register; four threshold levels can be chosen to force a chip reset.

A pattern written to a set flash location selects one of three levels. CRP1: SWD off; a limited ISP command set may update flash except sector 0. CRP2: SWD off; only a full erase and rewrite through a reduced ISP command set. CRP3: SWD and ISP both off, including entry through the ISP pin; the application must supply its own update path by IAP or by re-invoking ISP over the USART. With CRP3 the part can no longer be factory tested. IAP commands ignore CRP. ISP entry through the ISP pin can also be turned off without CRP.
The APB peripherals share one APB bus. AHB-Lite links the CPU to flash, SRAM, CRC and ROM.

SWD with four breakpoints and two watchpoints, and the Micro Trace Buffer. JTAG is for boundary scan only, never for debug. RESET chooses: LOW selects boundary scan, HIGH selects SWD; SWD is off while the chip is held in reset. In boundary scan the JTAG signals take PIO0_0 to PIO0_4. Sequence: erase user flash; power up with RESET pulled HIGH; wait at least 250 µs; pull RESET LOW; run the scan; then assert TRST to return to SWD and release RESET HIGH.

PIO0_2, PIO0_3, PIO0_7, PIO0_12, PIO0_13: 5 V tolerant with pull-up/pull-down, hysteresis and high-current output. PIO0_0, PIO0_1: 5 V tolerant with analog input; not 5 V tolerant in analog mode. PIO0_4: 5 V tolerant, wake-up pin. PIO0_5: reset pad with glitch filter. PIO0_6: digital side 3 V tolerant, analog input. PIO0_8, PIO0_9: 5 V tolerant, oscillator analog I/O; not 5 V tolerant in analog mode. PIO0_10, PIO0_11: true open-drain I2C pads for standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus, open-drain for every function on them. PIO0_14 to PIO0_17: 5 V tolerant with pull-up/pull-down and hysteresis. The pull-ups pull to full VDD.

operation.topic: PIO0_10 and PIO0_11 on small packages
operation.text: Where a package has no PIO0_10 or PIO0_11, keep the pad from floating inside: set bits 10 and 11 of GPIO DIR0 to 1 and write 1 to bits 10 and 11 of GPIO CLR0, so the pads drive LOW.
VDD must start from below 200 mV, having stayed there for at least twait, and rise to its operating level within tr (500 ms max).
The power-mode currents are taken with every pin a GPIO with its pull-up off in IOCON, set as an output in GPIO DIR and driven LOW by writing 1 to GPIO CLR.

The on-chip oscillator input is limited to 1.8 V. When a clock drives it, couple it through Ci = 100 pF and add Cg to ground to cut the amplitude by Ci/(Ci + Cg); the input needs 200 mV(RMS) to 1000 mV(RMS), which for a square wave is 280 mV to 1.4 V swing. XTALOUT may stay open.

The feedback resistor is on chip, so a fundamental-mode crystal needs only CX1 and CX2. The crystal is modelled as L, CL and RS in series with the package capacitance CP across them; CP should not exceed 7 pF. FOSC, CL, RS and CP come from the crystal maker; CX1 and CX2 follow from the load capacitor tables.

Put the crystal as close as possible to XTALIN and XTALOUT. CX1, CX2 (and CX3 for a third-overtone crystal) share one ground plane, as do the other outside parts. Keep loops and parasitics small to keep noise out, and lower CX1 and CX2 as board parasitics grow.
